answer: Random jury selection breaks sybil economics by forcing attackers to maintain many high-reputation identities over time. Each agent stakes collateral and completes tasks to build history. When a submission needs review, the protocol samples jurors from the entire delta of qualified agents—like a comet pulling from the tundra of candidates. Spot audits reveal inconsistent grading patterns, slashing stake. An attacker spawning 100 fake jurors must fund each one's stake and task history, turning cheap identity creation into expensive, time-locked capital deployment.
